blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At executive level, IT is not an enabler; it is a shaper. The company can only be what its systems allow it to be, and the boundaries of those systems quietly define the boundaries of the business. A company cannot scale faster than its infrastructure can carry it. It cannot serve customers better than its tools let it. It cannot take strategic risks that its data and its security posture cannot support.

The senior finance, commercial and product leaders who understand this treat the CIO as a peer, not a supplier. They bring IT into the room at the planning stage, not the implementation stage. And they take IT's constraints seriously, because those constraints, honestly understood, are part of what the company really is today.

The company whose strategy ignores its own IT reality is, eventually, a company surprised by what its own systems cannot do — usually at the worst possible moment.

items.q: According to the text, at executive level IT is best understood as…
items.why: "IT is not an enabler; it is a shaper" — no nível executivo, TI molda o que a empresa pode ser.

items.q: What do the leaders who understand this do differently?
options: They bring IT into the room only at the implementation stage
They keep IT constraints out of strategic discussions
They delegate strategy to the IT department
They treat the CIO as a peer and involve IT at the planning stage
items.why: "treat the CIO as a peer… bring IT into the room at the planning stage."

items.q: According to the text, why should leaders take IT's constraints seriously?
options: Because the CIO outranks other leaders
Because those constraints are part of what the company really is today
items.why: "those constraints, honestly understood, are part of what the company really is today."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: The CIO belongs in strategic planning conversations
A firm cannot grow faster than its infrastructure permits
IT merely executes decisions made elsewhere and has no shaping role
Strategy should be designed with IT's real limits in mind
items.why: Inferência: a tese central rejeita a ideia de que TI só executa — para o autor, TI molda os limites do negócio.

items.q: The final paragraph suggests that a company which ignores its IT reality will…
options: eventually be caught off guard by its own systems' limits at a critical moment
items.why: Inferência: "a company surprised by what its own systems cannot do — usually at the worst possible moment."

blocks.instruction: Ouça James defendendo a presença do CIO no offsite de estratégia. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Before we start, I want to say something about who's in this room. I've asked our CIO to join us today — not to present a slide at the end, but to sit here as a peer, from the first session to the last.

I know the instinct is to treat technology as something we hand over once the strategy is agreed. We decide what we want, and then we ask whether the systems can do it. In my experience, that sequence is exactly backwards. The systems are not a downstream detail; they are part of what we are today.

Watch what happens the moment she's in the conversation. When someone claims we can double the client base next year, she can tell us — honestly — whether the infrastructure carries that, or whether we are quietly promising something the platform cannot deliver. When we talk about a bolder risk appetite, she can tell us what our security posture actually supports.

That is not a constraint on ambition. It is the difference between a strategy we can execute and a wish list we discover, too late, we cannot. So I'd ask you to treat her contribution as strategy, not plumbing.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why has James asked the CIO to join the offsite?
options: To present a technical slide at the end
To take notes for the leadership team
To sit as a peer from the first session to the last
items.why: "not to present a slide at the end, but to sit here as a peer, from the first session to the last."

items.q: According to James, what is the usual — and wrong — sequence?
options: Building the systems before setting any goals
Deciding the strategy first, then asking whether the systems can do it
Letting IT set the company's ambitions
items.why: "We decide what we want, and then we ask whether the systems can do it… that sequence is exactly backwards."

items.q: What can the CIO tell the room when someone proposes doubling the client base?
options: When the next reorganisation should happen
Whether the infrastructure can actually carry that growth
items.why: "whether the infrastructure carries that, or whether we are quietly promising something the platform cannot deliver."

items.q: What does James mean by "a wish list we discover, too late, we cannot" execute?
options: A plan that looks good but the systems cannot actually support
A set of goals the board rejected
A list of features customers requested
A budget that was approved too quickly
items.why: Inferência: sem checar a realidade dos sistemas, a estratégia vira desejo impossível de entregar.

items.q: By ending with "treat her contribution as strategy, not plumbing," James implies that…
options: The CIO should focus only on maintenance
IT is a purely operational, behind-the-scenes matter
Technology decisions can wait until later
IT input shapes strategy and deserves equal standing in the discussion
items.why: Inferência: 'plumbing' (encanamento) seria papel secundário; James eleva a fala do CIO ao nível de estratégia.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Executives who see IT as a mere enabler underestimate its influence." An enabler is…
options: something that shapes what is possible from the outset
something that simply makes an existing goal easier to reach
items.why: Enabler = facilitador: apenas viabiliza o que já foi decidido — a lição argumenta que TI é mais que isso.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A firm cannot ___ faster than its infrastructure can carry it."
items.why: To scale = escalar, crescer em volume — limitado pela infraestrutura.

items.q: "They treat the CIO as a peer, not a supplier." A peer is…
items.why: Peer = par: alguém de igual estatura na mesa, não um fornecedor a quem se pede serviço.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "We cannot take a strategic risk that our ___ cannot support."
items.why: Security posture = postura de segurança: define quanto risco a empresa consegue de fato sustentar.

items.q: "IT's constraints, honestly understood, are part of what the company really is." Constraints are…
options: the limits within which the company must operate
items.why: Constraint = restrição: os limites reais que a estratégia precisa respeitar.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de estratégia e tecnologia. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The CIO still has to sign off on the platform migration." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the new system one region at a time." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Engineering pushed back on the aggressive timeline." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sinalizar objeção sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "None of these tweaks will move the needle on system reliability." This means they will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.

items.q: "Bring the CIO in early so IT concerns don't fall through the cracks." This means the concerns…
items.why: Fall through the cracks = passar despercebido, ser esquecido por falta de dono claro.
